title: Balalaika
summary: The balalaika is the triangular three-string lute of Russia. The common prima size is tuned E, E, A, with two strings on the same note and the third a fourth higher, and is played with quick finger strokes and strums.
howToPlay: Eight strings are shown side by side: A, B, C and D are played on the A string, E, F and G on the E strings, and the last lane is the full strum across all strings.
Each mark that falls onto the line is one note or strum; play that lane as it arrives.
Moving along a string by frets gives the neighbouring notes, so a short run climbs up the neck.
rules: The open strings are E, E and A; fretted notes in A minor fill in F and G on the E string and B, C and D on the A string.
Tunes are played twice through and keep one pulse: a dance tune in two, a slow waltz in three and a strum-and-answer pattern.
A note on the beat scores in full, a close one scores less, and an extra stroke costs a little.
heritageNote: The balalaika has been played in Russia for some three centuries by peasant musicians, accompanying songs and dances, and in the nineteenth century it was refined into a family of sizes for orchestras. The prima is held across the body and sounded with the side of the index finger.
